narrative: Material PL3__M207208F exhibits an erratic demand pattern (CV=0.59) with all 228 working days showing positive demand and no detectable trend; the bimodal intra-week profile (low-demand boundary days vs. high-demand core days) contributes to high variability. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.80, mean 1.15 days) with transport variability contributing 68% of total buffer variance, driving safety stock 69% above the current SAP setting. The recommended (r,Q) policy sets safety stock at 62,510 units and order quantity at 193,631 units (capacity-constrained from EOQ of 215,886), achieving a 95% service level at a modest annual cost premium of ~$693 over the current SAP configuration.
warnings: Capacity constraint is binding: order quantity reduced from EOQ 215,886 to 193,631 to satisfy max_storage_units=256,141. Post-replenishment stock exactly fills storage with near-zero headroom.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous (100% non-zero working days) with erratic but non-intermittent pattern, making a fixed reorder-point/fixed-quantity (r,Q) policy appropriate. EOQ provides the cost-minimising order size, and the normal-approximation safety stock formula is adequate given the moderate CV and large absolute volumes.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is fully utilised post-replenishment (256,141 of 256,141 units). Any demand shortfall before the next cycle completes will leave no buffer above safety stock; a single late shipment combined with above-average demand could cause a stockout. Recommend exploring capacity expansion or supplier lead time reduction to restore headroom.
